analysis: All three changed files are test-only: ProcessMemoryLedgerTests.swift (adds processLedgerCapacityShortfallIsTheBindingDeficit, lines 278-338), MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservationTests.swift (adds two shortfall-signal tests, lines 100-171) and ModelLoadEvictionAndAdmissionTests.swift (adds retainedSegmentsReleaseBeforeEviction, lines 88-113). No production source is in the supplied units, so no runtime control, trust boundary, key handling, or data flow changes in what I could see. The tests exercise memory-admission shortfall reporting and reclaim of retained KV segments before idle-model eviction. These relate loosely to T-028 (residual KV/GPU data) and T-041/TB-007 (prefix-cache KV segments retained in RAM), and to availability (T-010/T-029). The tests assert that retained parked bytes reach zero by the time a resident model shuts down, which supports the intended memory-hygiene behavior rather than weakening it. Test fixtures such as RetainingEngineStub, ParkedBytesRecorder and the MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation onRefusal initializer are not supplied. The production-side changes that implement shortfall reclaim (ProcessMemoryLedger.capacityShortfall, the onRefusal callback, the eviction-time release) were not reviewed. A later pass over those sources should check that reclaim cannot be triggered by a consumer to cause a DoS or cache-flush oracle, and that UInt64 overflow in the shortfall arithmetic is handled (the tests cover .max). No findings from these test files.
